disclaimer: Personal portfolio demo on synthetic data. Not financial, pricing or legal advice. The tool shows evidence and risk from past matters; a person decides the price.

inputs.cost_rates_note: PLACEHOLDER values for the demo only. Internal cost per hour by level is an input that finance must supply; these figures are invented and are not estimates of any firm's costs.
inputs.mapping: Synthetic export, shape A (four tidy files)

rules: Closed before 2026-01-01 (open matters are never comps).
Matters that closed abnormally (settled early, transferred, other) are excluded.
At least 8 comps are required before any figure is shown.

backtest.scope: Out of sample. Walk-forward back-test of every closed employment_single_plaintiff_defense matter, each modeled only from matters that closed before it opened, with the change check and the band adjustment also run as of that day. Matched on matter type only (not this proposal's selection rules), minimum 8 comps.
backtest.headline: Overruns at P75 and P90 are within what chance would explain at n=41.
backtest.verdict: Overruns at P75 and P90 are within what chance would explain at n=41. At the planning P75, 13 of 41 back-tested matters cost more; the band implies about 10. At the planning P90, 7 of 41 back-tested matters cost more; the band implies about 4. Costs appear to have fallen: the 11 matters opened from 2024-01-11 cost 0.63x the 55 opened before, at the same rates. A prompt to look, not a finding. Each planning band is the higher of the recent-only and whole-history versions, so the flag can raise a band but not lower it.

assumptions.text: Comps with a hearing (n=16) had a median cost of $231,700, 2.0x the median of comps without one ($117,100, n=50). Quote the hearing as a separate phase, or state that it is excluded.
The 17 comps above the P75 cost $277,500 more on average than the other 49. Discovery and diligence accounts for 28% of that gap ($77,600). Set a scope limit or a separate fee for that phase.

9 matters of this type closed abnormally (settled early, transferred or other) and are not in the comps. The figures assume the matter runs to completion; say what happens to the fee if it ends early.
The phase split for 4 of 66 comps comes from the date-window fallback, not task codes. Treat per-phase figures as lower confidence; totals are not affected.

Across the 66 comps, 12.4% of worked value was written down before billing and 2.5% of invoiced fees was not collected. A fee built from billed amounts would understate the work; the figures here use worked hours.

Costs for this matter type appear to have fallen: the 11 matters opened from 2024-01-11 cost 0.63x the 55 opened before, at the same rates (medians $95,800 and $151,800). The date is estimated from the data, and the check is a prompt to look, not a finding. This memo has not lowered the bands: each planning figure is the higher of the recent-only and whole-history versions. A person may choose the recent-only version (drift_action recent_only) after checking why. Both versions are shown below.
